mainTopic: אגדות about the ידיד, אברהם's plea at the חורבן, and the olive tree; then how the leavened מנחות are leavened without making the עשרון lacking or extra.
overview: This amud is mostly אגדה, and it ends by returning to הלכה. It finishes a poetic teaching where each ידיד ('beloved') stands for אברהם, the בית המקדש, הקדוש ברוך הוא, בנימין and ישראל. Two more teachings follow the same pattern, built on the words טוב and זה, and both describe משה receiving the תורה from הקדוש ברוך הוא for ישראל. רבי יצחק then tells how God found אברהם in the בית המקדש at the time of the חורבן. אברהם tries to defend his children, God answers every defense with words from ירמיהו, and a בת קול promises that ישראל, like an olive tree, will have a good end. The גמרא argues over the 'great tumult' in the פסוק: is it the spies' words, or God's pity, which shortened the rule of the four kingdoms? רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן draw two lessons from the olive tree: ישראל will never be wiped out, and suffering brings them back to good. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה about leavening the מנחות. It explains why outside starter dough can make the עשרון 'lacking or extra', and why the חכמים made a גזירה against a simpler method. It then begins a new ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Identifying the son of the beloved, the building beloved, and the One for whom it is built
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps decoding the ידיד statement. בן ידיד is אברהם, ויבנה ידיד is the בית המקדש, and לידיד is הקדוש ברוך הוא. Each identification has a פסוק that uses the word ידיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Son of a beloved' means אברהם, because a פסוק calls him 'My beloved'. 'And the beloved will build' means the בית המקדש, because a פסוק calls God's dwelling places 'lovely' (ידידות). 'For the Beloved' means הקדוש ברוך הוא, because a פסוק says 'Let me sing to my Beloved'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is going word by word through a poetic sentence that uses ידיד ('beloved') many times. For each ידיד, it names who is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ידיד in the sentence stands for a different figure. The proof is always a פסוק that uses a form of the word ידיד about that figure. So the sentence turns out to be about אברהם's descendant building the בית המקדש for הקדוש ברוך הוא.

keyTerms.meaning: Beloved one; the key word repeated throughout this teaching
The Holy One, Blessed be He (God)
Lovely, beloved (plural form, used about God's dwelling places)

steps.confusionAlert: The same word ידיד means a different figure each time it appears. Don't assume it always refers to the same person.

phrases.english: 'Son of a beloved one' – this is Abraham,
as it is written: 'What is My beloved doing in My house?'
'And will build a beloved thing' – this is the Holy Temple,
as it is written: 'How lovely are Your dwelling places'
'For the Beloved' – this is the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is written: 'Let me sing to my Beloved'

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן יָדִיד – זֶה אַבְרָהָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues decoding the ידיד statement, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן ידיד is אברהם, ויבנה ידיד is the בית המקדש, and לידיד is הקדוש ברוך הוא, each proven from a פסוק using the word ידיד.

steps.title: The portion of Binyamin and atonement for the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: The decoding of the ידיד statement ends here. 'In the portion of the beloved' is בנימין. 'The beloved ones who gain atonement' are ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the portion of the beloved' means בנימין, because משה blessed him as 'the beloved of ה׳'. 'And through it the beloved ones will be atoned for' means ישראל, because a פסוק calls them 'the beloved of My soul'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last two ידיד words in the sentence. This completes the whole ידיד teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בית המקדש is built in the חלק (portion) of בנימין, whom the תורה calls ידיד ה׳. ישראל, called ידידות נפשי, are the ones who gain כפרה through it. Read together, the sentence describes who builds the בית המקדש, where it stands, for whom it is built, and who benefits from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The beloved of My soul (a name for ישראל)

steps.whatToRemember: Every ידיד has been identified: אברהם, the בית המקדש, הקדוש ברוך הוא, בנימין and ישראל. The verse connects all of them to the building of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: 'In the portion of a beloved one' – this is Benjamin,
as it is stated: 'Of Benjamin he said:
The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by Him'
'And through it beloved ones will gain atonement' – these are the Jewish people,
as it is written: 'I have given the beloved of My soul
into the hand of her enemies.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יָדִיד – זֶה בִּנְיָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ידיד decoding that step 1 continued.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בחלקו של ידיד is בנימין, and the ידידים who gain atonement are ישראל.

steps.title: Let the good one receive the good from the Good for the good ones
steps.stepSummary: A new poetic statement repeats the word טוב. It is decoded as משה receiving the תורה from הקדוש ברוך הוא for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let the good one come and receive the good from the Good for the good ones.' The good one is משה, called טוב at his birth. The good he receives is the תורה, called 'good teaching'. The Good One is הקדוש ברוך הוא, who is 'good to all'. The good ones are ישראל, as the פסוק says 'Do good, ה׳, to the good ones'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching built on the same pattern as the ידיד one. This time the repeated word is טוב ('good').
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the full poetic line is stated, and then each טוב is matched to a figure through a פסוק. The theme moves from the בית המקדש to מתן תורה. משה is the one who receives, the תורה is what he receives, הקדוש ברוך הוא is the One who gives it, and ישראל are the ones it is for.

keyTerms.meaning: Good; the key word repeated in this teaching
Good teaching (a name for the תורה)

phrases.english: Let the good one come and receive the good
from the Good for the good ones.
'Let the good one come' – this is Moses,
as it is written: 'And she saw him, that he was good.'
phrases.notes: שמות 2:2. This is his mother looking at baby משה.

phrases.english: 'And receive the good' – this is the Torah,
as it is written: 'For I have given you good teaching.'
'From the Good' – this is the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is written: 'The Lord is good to all.'
'For the good ones' – these are the Jewish people,
as it is written: 'Do good, O Lord, to the good ones.'

steps.triggerLanguage: יָבֹא טוֹב וִיקַבֵּל טוֹב מִטּוֹב לַטּוֹבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching that follows the same word-repeating pattern as the ידיד teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The good one is משה, the good is the תורה, the Good is הקדוש ברוך הוא, and the good ones are ישראל.

steps.title: Let this one receive this from this One for this people
steps.stepSummary: A third poetic statement repeats the word זה/זאת/זו ('this'). Like the טוב teaching, it describes משה receiving the תורה from הקדוש ברוך הוא for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let this one come and receive this from this One for this people.' 'This one' is משה ('this משה, the man'). 'This' is the תורה ('this is the תורה'). 'This One' is הקדוש ברוך הוא ('this is my God'). 'This people' is ישראל ('this people that You acquired').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more teaching with the same pattern. This time the repeated word is 'this' (זה, זאת, זו).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The message is the same as in the טוב teaching: משה receives the תורה from הקדוש ברוך הוא for ישראל. Only the key word is different. Each 'this' is proven from a פסוק that uses the same form of the word about the same figure.
steps.whatToRemember: The three teachings share one structure: a key word is repeated, and each time it appears it points to a different figure, proven from a פסוק. The טוב and זה teachings both tell the story of מתן תורה: משה, the תורה, הקדוש ברוך הוא and ישראל.

phrases.english: Let this one come and receive this
from this One for this people –
'Let this one come' – this is Moses,
as it is written: 'For this Moses, the man'
'And receive this' – this is the Torah,
as it is written: 'And this is the Torah that Moses set'
'From this One' – this is the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is written: 'This is my God and I will glorify Him'
'For this people' – these are the Jewish people,
as it is stated: 'This people that You acquired.'

steps.triggerLanguage: יָבֹא זֶה וִיקַבֵּל זֹאת מִזֶּה לְעַם זוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel teaching to step 3, with the same message and a different key word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This one is משה, this is the תורה, this One is הקדוש ברוך הוא, and this people is ישראל.

steps.title: God finds אברהם standing in the destroyed Temple
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק opens a story. At the time of the חורבן, הקדוש ברוך הוא finds אברהם in the בית המקדש and asks, 'What is My beloved doing in My house?'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: When the בית המקדש was destroyed, הקדוש ברוך הוא found אברהם standing in it. He asked him: 'What is My beloved doing in My house?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that explains the פסוק 'מה לידידי בביתי', the same פסוק used earlier to show that ידיד means אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 only said that the ידיד in this פסוק is אברהם. Now רבי יצחק turns the whole פסוק and the next one into a conversation between God and אברהם. This opening question sets up everything that follows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
At the time when the Temple was destroyed,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, found Abraham
who was standing in the Temple.
He said to him: "What is My beloved doing in My house?"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 11:15. This is the same פסוק from earlier that showed ידיד means אברהם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ידיד פסוק from step 1 and expands it into a full story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'מה לידידי בביתי' is God speaking to אברהם in the בית המקדש at the time of the חורבן.

steps.title: אברהם came because of his children, who sinned and were exiled
steps.stepSummary: אברהם says he came because of his children. God answers that they sinned and were exiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said: I came about my children. God said: Your children sinned and went into exile.
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם explains why he is there, and God tells him the reason for the חורבן: the people sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the argument. God has given His reason for the גלות, and in the next steps אברהם will try to find a defense for ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ עַל עִיסְקֵי בָּנַי בָּאתִי,
phrases.english: He said to Him: I came about matters concerning my children.
He said to him: Your children sinned and were exiled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ עַל עִיסְקֵי בָּנַי בָּאתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers God's question from step 5 and gives the reason for the חורבן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is אברהם in the בית המקדש?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He came because of his children. God answers that they sinned and were exiled.

steps.title: They sinned on purpose, and most of them sinned
steps.stepSummary: אברהם suggests they sinned by mistake, or that only a few sinned. God rejects both with words from the פסוק: 'עשותה המזמתה' (on purpose) and 'הרבים' (the many).
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said: Maybe they sinned by mistake? God said: 'She carried out her wicked plan.' אברהם said: Maybe only a minority sinned? God said: 'The many.'
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם offers two defenses for ישראל, and God knocks down each one with a phrase from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first defense is that it was שוגג, a mistake. God answers that it was planned. The second defense is that only a few sinned. God answers that it was the majority. Each answer comes from a word of ירמיהו 11:15.

phrases.english: He said to Him: Perhaps they sinned by mistake?
He said to him: "She has carried out her wicked plan."
He said to Him: Perhaps only a minority of them sinned?
He said to him: "The many."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁמָּא בְּשׁוֹגֵג חָטְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אברהם challenges the reason God gave in step 6, and God rejects his challenges.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both of אברהם's defenses: that it was a mistake, and that only a few sinned.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק shows the sin was deliberate (מזמה) and done by the majority (רבים).

steps.title: The merit of ברית מילה and waiting for תשובה are both rejected
steps.stepSummary: אברהם asks God to remember ברית מילה, and suggests that waiting would have brought them to תשובה. God answers that they abandoned מילה, and that they enjoyed their sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said: You should have remembered the ברית מילה. God said: 'The holy flesh has passed away from you.' אברהם said: Maybe if You had waited, they would have done תשובה. God said: 'When you do evil, then you rejoice.'
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם tries two more defenses, and God again answers each one with a phrase from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The merit of ברית מילה cannot protect them, because they stopped keeping it. Waiting would not help either, because they were happy in their sin and would not have come back on their own.

phrases.english: You should have remembered the covenant of circumcision.
He said to him: "And the holy flesh has passed away from you."
phrases.notes: The holy flesh means the מילה. God is saying they had stopped keeping it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁמָּא אִם הִמְתַּנְתָּ לָהֶם
phrases.english: He said to Him: Perhaps if You had waited for them,
they would have come back in repentance.
He said to him: "When you do evil, then you rejoice."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה לְךָ לִזְכּוֹר בְּרִית מִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his first two defenses fail, אברהם tries two new ones, and they are rejected the same way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The merit of ברית מילה, and the idea that waiting would have led to תשובה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They had abandoned מילה, and they rejoiced in their sins instead of regretting them.

steps.title: אברהם cries: is there no hope for them?
steps.stepSummary: With all his defenses gone, אברהם puts his hands on his head, cries out, and asks whether ישראל have no repair at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away אברהם put his hands on his head, cried out and wept, and said: Could it be, חס ושלום, that they have no hope?
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם has run out of arguments, so he mourns and asks the deepest question: is this the end of ישראל? This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now אברהם was arguing about why the punishment came. Now he stops arguing about the past and asks about the future. Has the punishment closed the door for good?

keyTerms.meaning: a fix, a remedy, hope of repair

phrases.english: Immediately he placed his hands on his head,
and was crying out and weeping,
and he said to Him: Perhaps, Heaven forbid,
they have no remedy?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד הִנִּיחַ יָדָיו עַל רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: All of אברהם's defenses were rejected in steps 7-8, so now he despairs and asks about the future.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there any hope left for ישראל?

steps.title: The olive tree: ישראל's best comes at the end
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול answers with the next פסוק, which calls ישראל an olive tree. Just as an olive tree's best comes at its end, ישראל's best will come at their end.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת קול came out and said: 'ה׳ called your name a fresh olive tree, beautiful with fine fruit.' Just as an olive tree's best comes at its end, so too ישראל's best comes at their end.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with hope. A heavenly voice answers אברהם with the next פסוק and promises that ישראל have a good ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An olive tree gives its real value, its fruit and oil, at the very end. So too ישראל: even after the חורבן and גלות, their final destiny is good. This answers אברהם's question in step 9 with a clear yes, there is hope.

keyTerms.meaning: its best (its final purpose) comes at its end

steps.whatToRemember: אברהם's defenses for ישראל all fail: the sin was on purpose, done by the many, ברית מילה was abandoned, and they enjoyed their sins. But the story ends with a promise: like an olive tree, ישראל's best comes at the end.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story turns the ידיד פסוק from a picture of punishment into a message of hope that ישראל will return in the end.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said to him:
"A fresh olive tree, beautiful with fine fruit,
ה׳ called your name."
Just as this olive tree,
phrases.notes: Some versions say זו and others say זה. Both just mean 'this'.

phrases.english: its best comes at its end,
so too ישראל, their best comes at their end.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אברהם's question from step 9 and closes the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ישראל have not lost their future. Like an olive tree, their best will come at the end.

steps.title: The spies' words broke ישראל's branches
steps.stepSummary: רבי חיננא בר פפא reads 'the sound of a great tumult' as the sound of the spies' words, which broke ישראל's branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'With the sound of a great tumult He set fire to it, and its branches are broken.' רבי חיננא בר פפא says: because of the sound of the spies' words, ישראל's branches were broken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last part of the olive-tree פסוק. רבי חיננא בר פפא explains that the 'tumult' was the spies' report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the word המולה as if it came from מילין, meaning 'words'. So the damage to ישראל (the broken branches) goes back to what the מרגלים said in the desert.

keyTerms.meaning: The spies משה sent to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: "With the sound of a great tumult
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 11:16, the same olive-tree פסוק from the last step.

phrases.english: He has set fire to it, and its branches are broken."
Rabbi Chinnana bar Pappa says:
From the sound of the words of the spies
phrases.notes: He hears הֲמוּלָּה as sounding like מִילִּין, which means 'words'.

phrases.english: the branches of ישראל were broken.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִינָּנָא בַּר פָּפָּא: לְקוֹל מִילֵּיהֶן שֶׁל מְרַגְּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same פסוק that the בת קול quoted in step 10, now explaining its last words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'great tumult' in the פסוק is the spies' words, which broke ישראל's branches.

steps.title: What made the spies' words so terrible
steps.stepSummary: רבי חיננא בר פפא shows how serious the spies' words were. They hinted that the Canaanites were stronger than God Himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חיננא בר פפא said: the spies said a terrible thing at that moment. 'He is stronger than us.' Do not read it as 'than us'. Read it as 'than Him'. They meant, so to speak, that even the Owner of the house cannot take His things out of there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from the same רבי חיננא בר פפא. It backs up why the spies' words could cause such great damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ממנו can mean 'than us' or 'than him'. Reading it as 'than Him' means the spies were denying God's power. That explains why their words could 'break the branches' of ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not read it as...'. This is a way of reading a word in a second way to learn something new
So to speak, as it were (used when speaking about God in human terms)
The owner of the house (here, God)

steps.confusionAlert: The spies did not literally say 'stronger than God'. The words of the פסוק stay the same. The 'do not read' method only shows the hidden meaning of what they were saying.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chinnana bar Pappa says:
The spies said a serious thing
at that moment:
"For he is stronger than us."
Do not read it as "than us" but as "than Him,"
phrases.notes: The same Hebrew word can mean either 'than us' or 'than him'.

phrases.english: as it were,
meaning that even the Owner of the house
cannot take His belongings out of there.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִינָּנָא בַּר פָּפָּא: דָּבָר גָּדוֹל דִּבְּרוּ מְרַגְּלִים בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 11 by showing how serious the spies' words were.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the spies' words could 'break the branches' of ישראל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reading of 'ממנו' in במדבר 13:31 as 'stronger than Him'

steps.title: The word is המולה, not מלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא, son of רבי חיננא, challenges his father's reading. If the פסוק meant 'words', it should have said מלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא son of רבי חיננא challenged this: this phrase says 'the sound of a great המולה'. If it meant words, it should have said 'the sound of a מלה (word)'!
steps.whatsHappening: A son challenges his father's explanation from the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading in step 11 depends on המולה meaning 'words'. But the word for 'word' is מלה. So why would the פסוק use the longer word המולה? That suggests it means something else.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרַבִּי חִינָּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya son of Rabbi Chinnana challenges it:
This phrase, "With the sound of a great tumult,"
it should have said "With the sound of a word"!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרַבִּי חִינָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of המולה given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חיננא בר פפא's reading of המולה as the spies' words
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק meant 'words', it would have used the simple word מלה, not המולה.

steps.title: God took pity after אברהם's plea
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא reads המולה as חמלתי, 'I took pity'. Because of אברהם's voice, God shortened the time ישראל would serve the four kingdoms.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, הקדוש ברוך הוא said to אברהם: I heard your voice and I took pity on them. I had said they would be enslaved to four kingdoms, and each one would last as long as all four together. Now each one will last only the time set for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא gives his own reading. He ties the פסוק back to the conversation between אברהם and God from the earlier steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads המולה as coming from חמל, 'pity'. The 'voice' is אברהם's cry from step 9. The result: the original plan was for each kingdom to rule for the length of all four together. Now each rules only for its own share, so the exile is much shorter.

keyTerms.meaning: The four kingdoms that ruled over ישראל

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאַבְרָהָם:
phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Abraham:
I heard your voice
and I took pity on them.
phrases.notes: Here הֲמוּלָּה is heard as חָמַלְתִּי, 'I took pity'.

phrases.english: I had said they would be enslaved to four kingdoms,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת כְּשִׁיעוּר אַרְבַּע מַלְכִיּוֹת.
phrases.english: each one for the length of all four kingdoms.
Now, each one
only what was set for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאַבְרָהָם: קוֹלְךָ שָׁמַעְתִּי וְחָמַלְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading that step 13 rejected with a new reading tied to אברהם's plea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of אברהם's cry, God shortened the exile: each kingdom rules only for its own share, not for the time of all four.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that אברהם's cry in step 9 was not for nothing. Even after every argument was turned down, his prayer still made the exile easier.

steps.title: Another version: all at once instead of one after another
steps.stepSummary: Some say God's pity worked differently: the kingdoms would rule at the same time instead of one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say God told him: I had said the kingdoms would rule one after the other. Now they will rule all at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what God's pity changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the length of each kingdom's rule stays the same. Instead, the kingdoms overlap in time, in different places, so the whole exile ends sooner.

phrases.english: And some say:
I had said one after the other,
now, all at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of what God's pity in step 14 changed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's pity made the four kingdoms rule at the same time, shortening the exile.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that אברהם's cry made God take pity and shorten the exile. They only disagree on how: shorter rule for each kingdom, or all kingdoms ruling together.

steps.title: Like an olive tree: ישראל never fall away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי: just as an olive tree's leaves never fall, ישראל will never be wiped out, in this world or the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says: Why are ישראל compared to an olive tree? To teach you: just as an olive tree's leaves do not fall, not in summer and not in the rainy season, so too ישראל will never be wiped out, not in this world and not in the next world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the comparison of ישראל to an olive tree in the פסוק, and gives a first lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An olive tree stays green all year. רבי יהושע בן לוי learns from this that ישראל last forever, in both worlds. This fits the comfort the בת קול gave in step 10.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
Why were ישראל compared to an olive tree?
To tell you:
just as an olive tree's leaves do not fall,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וְלֹא בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים,
phrases.english: not in the summer and not in the rainy season,

phrases.aramaic: אַף יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין לָהֶם בְּטֵילָה עוֹלָמִית,
phrases.english: so too ישראל will never be wiped out,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: not in this world and not in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְזַיִת? לוֹמַר לְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the olive-tree image in the פסוק and draws a new lesson from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראל, like the evergreen olive tree, will never be wiped out.

steps.title: Like an olive tree: crushing brings out the best
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן: just as an olive gives its oil only when crushed, ישראל return to the right path only through suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: Why are ישראל compared to an olive tree? To teach you: just as an olive gives out its oil only when it is crushed, so too ישראל return to the good path only through suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: A second lesson from the same olive-tree comparison, this time about why ישראל suffer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil does not come from a whole olive. It has to be pressed. רבי יוחנן learns from this that suffering is what brings ישראל back to good. This also explains the hard exile described in the steps before.
steps.whatToRemember: The olive tree teaches two lessons. רבי יהושע בן לוי: ישראל will never be wiped out. רבי יוחנן: suffering is what brings out ישראל's best and brings them back to good.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְזַיִת? לוֹמַר לְךָ:
phrases.english: Why were ישראל compared to an olive tree? To tell you:
just as an olive does not give out its oil
except by being crushed,
so too ישראל do not return to the good path
except through suffering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second lesson from the same olive-tree comparison as step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Like an olive that gives oil only when crushed, ישראל return to good only through suffering.

steps.title: Quoting רבי מאיר's view on the leaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי מאיר says the starter dough is taken from the מנחה's own flour and used to leaven it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: the leaven is separated from the flour of the מנחות themselves, and they are leavened with it, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some מנחות must be baked as חמץ, so they need a starter. רבי מאיר says to take some of the measured flour itself, let it sour, and use it to leaven the rest. The 'וכו׳' points to the rest of the משנה, where רבי יהודה disagrees and the חכמים say his way leaves the measure 'lacking or extra'.

keyTerms.meaning: Sourdough starter, a piece of soured dough used to make other dough rise
Separates or takes out a portion
From within them, meaning from the מנחה's own flour

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
The leaven: one separates it for them from within them
and leavens them with it, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: רבי יהודה brings the leaven from outside, and the חכמים say that makes it 'lacking or extra'.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (as the lead-in to the question)
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: הַשְּׂאוֹר בּוֹדֶה לָהֶן מִתּוֹכָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic olive-tree teachings and returns to the משנה's halachic discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the starter for a חמץ מנחה comes from the מנחה's own flour.

steps.title: What does 'lacking or extra' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חכמים meant when they said רבי יהודה's method makes the מנחה 'lacking or extra'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'lacking or extra' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the חכמים's objection to רבי יהודה. How exactly would bringing outside leaven throw off the measure?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is unclear. Why would outside leaven sometimes make it too little and sometimes too much? The גמרא wants a concrete explanation of both possibilities.

keyTerms.meaning: Lacking, less than the required amount
Extra, more than the required amount

phrases.english: What is meant by "lacking or extra"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״חֲסֵירָה אוֹ יְתֵירָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the part of the משנה quoted in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How bringing leaven from outside could make the מנחה's flour less than or more than one עשרון.

steps.title: רב חסדא: stiff starter means too much, soft starter means too little
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that it depends on how thick the outside starter dough is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: if the starter dough is stiff, the total comes out more than an עשרון. If it is soft, it comes out less.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The amount of water in the outside starter makes the total flour come out wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stiff dough has little water, so it takes up little room. More fresh flour is needed to fill the measure, so the total flour is too much. A soft dough has lots of water and takes up more room. Less fresh flour fits in, so the total flour is too little.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, the set measure of flour for a מנחה

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
If the starter dough is stiff,
it turns out to be more than the measure of an עשרון;
phrases.notes: Stiff dough is small for the flour in it, so more fresh flour is needed to fill the measure.

phrases.english: if it is soft, it turns out to be lacking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: עִיסַּת הַשְּׂאוֹר עָבֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Extra' happens with a stiff starter and 'lacking' happens with a soft starter, because the water changes how much room the starter takes in the measure.

steps.title: But he fills a full עשרון anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא: whatever the starter is like, the person fills the measuring vessel to a full עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, when he measures, he measures to a full עשרון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חסדא. Why should stiff or soft matter if the vessel ends up full either way?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes the measure is simply whatever fills the vessel right now, starter plus fresh flour. If so, the result is always exactly one עשרון, and there is no 'lacking or extra'.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, ultimately: used to say 'whatever happens, the result is the same'

phrases.english: In the end,
when he measures,
he measures out a full עשרון.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, כִּי קָא כָיֵיל לְעִשָּׂרוֹן קָא כָיֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's explanation from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that a stiff or soft starter makes the measure extra or lacking.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vessel is filled to the top either way, so the total is always exactly one עשרון. The thickness of the starter should not matter.

steps.title: The measure counts the flour as it was before water
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף explain that the עשרון is figured by the starter's original flour, not by its present size as dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: we measure according to what they originally were.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה and רב יוסף answer the challenge. The measure counts the flour that went into the starter, not how much room the wet dough takes now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said a full vessel is always an עשרון. The answer is that the real measure is the amount of flour. Once water is in the starter, its size no longer shows how much flour is in it. So filling the vessel can leave the true flour too much or too little, and רב חסדא's point stands.

keyTerms.meaning: According to how they are or were: here, the original state of the flour

steps.whatToRemember: A מנחה's עשרון is a measure of flour. When outside starter dough is used, its water hides how much flour it really holds, so the total can come out lacking or extra.

phrases.english: Rabbah and Rav Yosef, who both say:
We measure it according to what they were.
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets appears in the printed גמרא, but some versions leave it out. Either way, it means 'as they were before water was added'.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהֵן הָיְתָה מְשַׁעֲרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 and so supports רב חסדא's explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what is being measured: original flour, not present size.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A vessel filled to the top always holds exactly one עשרון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עשרון is figured by the flour as it was before water was added, so a starter's present size can make the true flour lacking or extra.

steps.title: Why not leaven a piece of the measured flour separately?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a simple method: take a bit from the measured עשרון, leaven it outside, and knead it back in. This seems to avoid the 'lacking or extra' problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him take a little from it, leaven it outside, then bring it and knead it together with the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes an easy way to get a perfectly measured, leavened מנחה, and asks why the חכמים don't allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים rejected רבי יהודה's method because an outside starter could make the עשרון too little or too much. If the starter is taken from the עשרון that was already measured, the amount stays exact. So the חכמים seem to have no reason to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: outside, separately from the main dough
let him knead it (from לִישָׁה, kneading)

phrases.english: But let him take a little from it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the flour of the עשרון after it was already measured exactly.

phrases.english: and leaven it outside,
and bring it and knead it together with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִישְׁקוֹל פּוּרְתָּא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the 'lacking or extra' concern of the חכמים, the גמרא proposes a method that seems to avoid that concern entirely.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's position that leavening must be done only in the way described in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the starter comes from the already-measured עשרון, it cannot be lacking or extra, so there seems to be no reason to forbid this method.

steps.title: A safeguard against bringing starter from outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this method is forbidden because of a גזירה: people might come to bring starter dough from elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case people come to bring it from elsewhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the simple method is not allowed: the חכמים made a protective rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strictly speaking, the method would work. But someone watching a separate leavened piece being added might think any outside starter is fine. They might then bring starter dough that was never part of the מנחה flour, so the חכמים forbade the whole practice.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
from elsewhere, from an outside source

steps.whatToRemember: The method of leavening a piece of the measured flour separately would work, but the חכמים forbade it as a safeguard. Otherwise people might bring starter from outside the מנחה.

phrases.english: It is a decree,
lest he come to bring it from elsewhere.
phrases.notes: He means starter dough that was never part of this מנחה's flour.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה, דִּלְמָא אָתֵי לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מֵעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since taking starter from the measured עשרון keeps the amount exact, it should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden as a גזירה, so that people won't come to use starter from outside sources.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about leavening the מנחות begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא that starts with the words 'One may not leaven'. The rest of it continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: One may not leaven…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it starts quoting a ברייתא about how the leavened מנחות may be leavened. The rest of the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This begins a new topic within the same subject of leavened מנחות. So far we only know that the ברייתא is about to forbid some way of leavening. The details come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: one leavens (makes the dough rise into חָמֵץ)

phrases.english: The Sages taught: One may not leaven

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מַחְמִיצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the leavening debate to a new ברייתא on the same subject.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of a ברייתא restricting how the leavened מנחות may be leavened. The ruling continues beyond this text.
